question: please provide details on the technical and organizational security measures the vendor has in place to provide and enforce the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and/or services.
details: danfe corp follows a comprehensive security approach to ensure the protection of user data. this approach includes technical and organizational measures to safeguard personal data. we have a documented information security policy that aligns with soc 2 type 2 guidelines. our information security policy defines a data classification policy based on the risk and sensitivity of the data. we have clear definitions of security roles and responsibilities. danfe corp has a dedicated information security team and they review the information security policies and risk management program at least once a year. we have role-based access control and abide by "need-to-know" guidelines. only a few members of the engineering team have access to the production environment where customer data is stored. all data in transit is encrypted using tls 1.3 and tls 1.2. every communication takes place over https requests, and the insecure http protocol is automatically redirected to use the secure https protocol. all data is encrypted utilizing the capabilities of aws rds, s3, and ebs to encrypt data at rest and in storage using aes-256.

question: is there a patch management program in place to ensure that patches are implemented timely for all devices, systems, and software? please describe your patch management program or provide a copy of the program.
details:
the danfe corp patch management process includes security, application, and operation system patches. danfe corp has a documented patch management policy. at danfe corp, once a patch is released, and the associated security vulnerability is reviewed and assessed for its applicability and importance, the patch is applied and verified in a time frame that is commensurate with the risk posed to systems:
- for critical risks: patches are applied as soon as possible, and we aim to mitigate within 24 hours and remediate within 7 days.
- for major risks: we aim to mitigate as needed and approved by the security team and remediate within 14 days.
- for minor and trivial risks: we remediate within 60 days and with the best effort, respectively. danfe corp relies on a third-party vendor to perform security and vulnerability scans and penetration testing annually. internal penetration testing is performed on an annual basis.

details:
the danfe corp patch management process includes security, application, and operation system patches. danfe corp has a documented patch management policy. at danfe corp, once a patch is released, and the associated security vulnerability is reviewed and assessed for its applicability and importance, the patch is applied and verified in a time frame that is commensurate with the risk posed to systems:
- for critical risks: patches are applied as soon as possible, and we aim to mitigate within 24 hours and remediate within 7 days.
- for major risks: we aim to mitigate as needed and approved by the security team and remediate within 14 days.

question: do you have a procedure to keep track of the announcement of vulnerability patches for your networking devices? please describe the procedure.

the danfe corp patch management process includes security, application, and operation system patches. danfe corp has a documented patch management policy. at danfe corp, once a patch is released, and the associated security vulnerability is reviewed and assessed for its applicability and importance, the patch is applied and verified in a time frame that is commensurate with the risk posed to systems:
- for critical risks: patches are applied as soon as possible, and we aim to mitigate within 24 hours and remediate within 7 days.
- for major risks: we aim to mitigate as needed and approved by the security team and remediate within 14 days.
- for minor and trivial risks: we remediate within 60 days and with the best effort, respectively.

question: how long do openai and other 3rd party model providers store my data?

openai and our other third-party model providers store data temporarily, or in some cases not at all, to process requests and enable the ai features. they are not permitted to use this data for training their own models. the openai api endpoints that currently power ai beta features are subject to the default openai data retention policies. data is temporarily retained in openai’s environment for up to 30 days to provide the services and identify abuse. please refer to openai’s api data policy page for more information:
https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/
similarly, microsoft azure's openai service retains data for up to 30 days to provide the
services and identify abuse. please see azure's api data policy page for more information: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/cognitive-services/openai/data-privacy?tabs=azure-portal
where possible, danfe corp enables openai’s zero data retention (zdr) option for approved use cases like the current figjam ai beta features to reduce the amount of data retained by openai, but we cannot guarantee that zdr will be available for future features.
our other model providers, jasper and aws, do not retain data after processing.

- twelve (12) characters minimum length
- upper case letter & lower case letter
- number (0-9) & symbol (i.e. !@#$%^&*)
- does not contain part of the username
- does not contain first name and last name
- is not a common password
- password expires after 365 days
- new passwords must not be the same as the last twenty-four (24) passwords

- does not contain part of the username

before you can access an endpoint within danfe corp, you will need to provide valid authentication. you can authenticate your request to the danfe corp api in two ways:
- generate a personal access token through your user profile page. this gives you access to the danfe corp api as if you were a single user.

question: is unencrypted restricted/secret data included in the message body or as an attachment in email communications?
details:
danfe corp is a saas platform, and access to design files can be shared via a public link that has password enforcement and an expiration policy set to it. danfe corp uses sendgrid, inc. for cloud-based email notification services, but emailing is not a part of the platform's functionality. additionally, data in transit is encrypted via tls 1.2 (or higher) when traversing public networks. customers can navigate to https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/ to test the encryption algorithms of their own danfe corp instance.
customer fig at rest is encrypted via aes-256. rds backups and logs maintained by danfe corp are stored in offsite s3 buckets, encrypted via aes 256.
emails are sent as notifications to users who opt-in. the email in transit is encrypted, and access to user email accounts is required to review where the client security controls apply.

details:
internally danfe corp follows nist best practices for password management. for single sign-on systems (i.e., okta) danfe corp enforces the following password requirements:
- twelve (12) characters minimum length.
- upper case letter & lower case letter.
- number (0-9) & symbol (i.e. !@#$%^&*)
- does not contain part of the username
- does not contain first name and last name.
- is not a common password
- password expires after 365 days.
- new passwords must not be the same as the last twenty-four (24) passwords.
- locks out users after 6 unsuccessful password attempts - systems must be accessed through mfa and require device trust + biometric factor to access.
passwords would be changed in accordance with this.

2. danfe corp seeks to refer each government request promptly to the relevant customer or user so that the customer or user can respond directly.

question: danfe corp does not offer customer-supported keys or private clouds. how does danfe corp ensure the security of logical isolation?
details:
danfe corp relies on a multi-layer defensive model. these are:
- we provide centralized api and access control logic for most central application logic (new features might do something on their own while they iterate on it and later move to centralized logic). we use a graphql-like service to centralize this logic (we call it live graph)
- new features typically require negative tests around access control. this prevents future regressions.
- all identifiers used for access are long unguessable random strings. this means that even in the case of an access control issue, an attacker cannot easily find or exploit them (they need to know the unguessable number)
- rate limits and alerts on anomalous activity will alert us on any large-scale access control issue
- we additionally run consistency checkers/invariant checkers in the background on our logs to make sure that access decisions were appropriate and not breaking key invariants (e.g., all membership in an organization had a valid, approved reason for it)
- organizations can layer their own defenses on top: default link sharing can be disabled.
- all org activity is logged in the activity logs. organizations can layer defenses on top to make sure that activity matches their patterns (e.g., activity from user alice matches the ip that they see on their sso and other saas providers as
well as there is no activity from weird countries)
- finally, in case of any issue, we have additional logs of requests and any file access (and client-side logging) that let us clearly understand the impact and if any data was affected.

question:

(1)  vendor shall have appointed a personal information manager or the like

(4) vendor shall have the means to verify the conditions of handling personal information

details:
(1) danfe corp has a head of security ciso in place who is responsible for overseeing the security policy. we also have a dedicated information security team. the security organization consists of the director of security and the compliance officer.
(2) danfe corp has a security training program for employees. the program includes mandatory training for all new hires, annual participation for existing employees, and role-based training. the training covers various topics such as information security rules and policies, personal accountability and responsibilities, password security, and contact points for escalating security and privacy issues. there are consequences for violating data security policies.
(3) we have a formal privacy policy that is reviewed annually. for additional details please see our privacy policy: https://www.danfe corp.com/privacy/
(4) danfe corp has a policy regarding the handling of personal information (pi), including the principles of data minimization, restriction of disclosure, secure storage, and destruction. (5) danfe corp has its own logging and monitoring system for internal security. all security events from all systems are logged. all access to platforms, applications, and databases is subject to approval and audit logging. logs are maintained for different periods depending on the system. audit logs are protected from unauthorized access and resistant to attacks including deactivation, modification, or deletion.
(6) danfe corp uses a firewall within the aws virtual private cloud (vpc) as a protection mechanism to prevent access to or alteration of any information asset by unauthorized personnel. we use security groups (which act as a virtual firewall for our instance to control inbound and outbound traffic) and monitor them continuously to ensure that only approved resources and approved ports are on the internet. danfe corp has a signature and/or anomaly-based ids/ips in place, and sensors are in place at strategic points throughout the network. it is employed in all available network zones. it includes system monitoring. an intrusion detection system (ids) is utilized to analyze network events and report potential network security breaches. the ids is configured to notify appropriate personnel upon intrusion detection. we also utilize amazon cloudfront, which includes the aws shield web application firewall (waf). additionally, we rely on the default content & email filter capabilities of chrome/safari/firefox browsers as well as the email filtering capabilities of gmail.

question: describe your inline email security controls
details:
our organization's inline email security controls are designed to protect our email communications from various threats, including phishing attacks, malware, spam, and data leakage. we employ a multi-layered approach to ensure the security and integrity of our email system. our inline email security controls include:

email filtering: we use advanced email filtering solutions to scan incoming and outgoing emails for malicious content, suspicious attachments, and known threats. this filtering process helps prevent spam and phishing emails from reaching our users' inboxes.

anti-malware scanning: our inline email security system incorporates real-time anti-malware scanning to detect and quarantine any malicious attachments or links within emails. this helps to prevent malware from spreading through our email infrastructure.

phishing protection: we utilize anti-phishing technologies that analyze email content and sender information to identify phishing attempts. suspicious emails are flagged or quarantined for further review.

url filtering: to protect against malicious links, our system scans and categorizes urls embedded in emails. it blocks access to known malicious websites and warns users when they click on potentially harmful links.

data loss prevention (dlp): we have implemented dlp rules that automatically identify and prevent the unauthorized transmission of sensitive or confidential data through email. this helps us maintain data security and compliance with regulatory requirements.

email encryption: for sensitive and confidential communications, we use email encryption to protect the content of messages in transit. this ensures that only authorized recipients can access the information.

authentication and sender verification: we implement authentication protocols such as spf, dkim, and dmarc to verify the authenticity of incoming emails and prevent domain spoofing. this helps reduce the likelihood of receiving forged or phishing emails.

real-time threat intelligence: our email security controls are continuously updated with threat intelligence feeds and signatures to stay ahead of emerging threats. this proactive approach helps us identify and block new threats in real time.

user awareness and training: we also place emphasis on user awareness and training programs to educate our employees about email security best practices. this includes recognizing phishing attempts and avoiding risky email behavior.

incident response: in the event of a security incident, we have well-defined incident response procedures in place to investigate, contain, and mitigate the impact of any email-related security breaches.

question: is the data fully encrypted and is the key exclusively held by a client entity or a trusted entity within the eu/eea?

encryption transforms data into a form that can no longer be accessed by unauthorized persons. the data can only be accessed again after the data has been decrypted with the correct key.
please note that personal data only qualifies as completely encrypted if the data is permanently completely encrypted both during transmission and at rest, as well as during the processing itself.
insofar as data is stored by the hosting service provider without being continuously processed, "encryption during processing" and "encryption at rest" are identical.

question: do you perform security assessments of third-party companies with which you share data (i.e. hosting providers, cloud services, paas, iaas, saas, etc.)?
details:
danfe corp has a vendor management program for selecting and overseeing the third-party services that danfe corp relies upon as part of normal business operations. the review considers risk factors such as the sensitivity of data stored in the service; the criticality of danfe corp's dependency on the service; and the reputation and history of the service, e.g. for reliability.
the vendor assessment consists of a review of the service's privacy policies and terms of service or negotiated service agreement for assertions that the service will protect and secure the data stored on the service. particularly, we look for:
a) the service will not sell, rent, transfer, distribute, or otherwise make available data stored on the service except for providing the service or for other limited reasons such as for complying with applicable laws and
b) that the service will take reasonable measures to secure data stored in the service.
the vendor assessment also includes a review of the vendor's information security practices which includes the following (depending on what information is made available by the vendor): soc 2 report; responses to a questionnaire submitted by danfe corp to vendors; and/or security-related information content published online by the vendor. vendors are reviewed on a yearly cadence and the review process is revised on an ongoing basis.

question: do the procedures of a cloud service provider ensure that governmental agencies, in the context of investigation requests, are restricted to accessing or gaining insight into only the data that is the specific subject of the request? if clear data limitations are not feasible, does the cloud service provider anonymize or pseudonymize the data to restrict government agencies from assigning it to any cloud customer not subject to the investigation request?
details:
if danfe corp did receive a government request to access or disclose our customer’s data it would adhere to the danfe corp privacy principles in responding. these principles are as follows:
1. danfe corp will retain and, as appropriate, consult with expert legal counsel regarding all third-party requests for customer data.
2. danfe corp seeks to refer each government request promptly to the relevant customer or user so that the customer or user can respond directly.
3. if the government declines to redirect its request to the relevant customer, danfe corp will provide the customer with prompt notice of the request unless it is legally prohibited from doing so.
4. if danfe corp is prohibited from providing prompt notice of a request to a customer, danfe corp provides such notice as soon as the prohibition expires or is no longer in effect.
5. danfe corp publishes and annually updates a transparency report that provides customers with information regarding the number and types of government requests for customer data it receives and how it responds to them.
6. danfe corp assesses the legality of all such requests and complies with requests only if and to the extent it assesses that they are valid, lawful, and compulsory.
7. danfe corp will decline to comply with and undertake reasonable efforts to contest any request it determines is not required by applicable law, including any non-valid request under fisa 702 or u.s. executive order 12333.

question: provide brief details of how your network is protected and managed to ensure its security.

danfe corp uses security groups (which act as a virtual firewall for our instance to control inbound and outbound traffic) and monitors them continuously to ensure that only approved resources and approved ports are on the internet. danfe corp has a signature and/or anomaly-based ids/ips in place, and sensors are in place at strategic points throughout the network. it is employed in all available network zones. it includes system monitoring. an intrusion detection system (ids) is utilized to analyze network events and report potential network security breaches. the ids is configured to notify appropriate personnel upon intrusion detection.

danfe corp performs penetration testing and manual code reviews before releasing applications and apis to production. we use a third-party vendor to perform annual vulnerability and penetration testing. all internet-facing networks and systems go through rigorous vulnerability scans. we use automated continuous code scanning to detect any known vulnerabilities. we also run detectify, a network web application scanner that scans the web application for open ports, cloud issues, as well as any owasp issues every week. additionally, danfe corp uses both ips and ids, and also there is a firewall to monitor the network and system for malicious activity.
the timeframe for addressing the vulnerabilities is based on their criticality as follows:
- for critical risks: patches are applied as soon as possible, and we aim to mitigate within 24 hours and remediate within 7 days.
- for major risks: we aim to mitigate as needed and approved by the security team, and remediate within 14 days.
- for minor and trivial risks: we remediate within 60 days and with the best effort, respectively.

question: what would danfe corp do if it received a government access request in respect to customer personal data?
details:
if danfe corp did receive a government request to access or disclose our customer’s personal data it would adhere to the danfe corp privacy principles in providing a response. these principles are as follows:
1. danfe corp will retain and, as appropriate, consult with expert legal counsel regarding all third-party requests for customer data.
2. danfe corp seeks to refer each government request promptly to the relevant customer or user so that the customer or user can respond directly.
3. if the government declines to redirect its request to the relevant customer, danfe corp will provide the customer with prompt notice of the request unless it is legally prohibited from doing so.
4. if danfe corp is prohibited from providing prompt notice of a request to a customer, danfe corp provides such notice as soon as the prohibition expires or is no longer in effect.
5. danfe corp publishes and annually updates a transparency report that provides customers with information regarding the number and types of government requests for customer data it receives and how it responds to them.
6. danfe corp assesses the legality of all such requests and complies with requests only if and to the extent it assesses that they are valid, lawful, and compulsory.
7. danfe corp will decline to comply with and undertake reasonable efforts to contest any request it determines is not absolutely required by applicable law, including any non-valid request under fisa 702 or u.s. executive order 12333.

question: do danfe corp employees have admin access?
details:
danfe corp employees have "admin" on our all mac fleet on the corp side; not on production where customer data resides. "admin" in quotes is that we still have a "super admin" that is running our management and security software. even if users have admin, they can't disable our security tooling.
macs also have system integrity protection and such checks which means that the “admin” is a lot more restricted than the classic admin on unix or windows. zoom, dropbox, etc still require basic admin privileges. this allows fixing up sound, video camera, etc. but this doesn't let a user affect our security controls. we can still technically kick out a user from the network as well as remote wipe as needed via our controls. finally, in case of any issue, employees do not have any privileged access just because of being on the corp network or machine. data access is typically through centrally managed sso or gsuite login and we can kick out employees as needed from it; so as a secondary layer of control, even if the local wipe of an employee fails, they won't be able to access anything if we disable their gsuite and okta accounts.

question: what is done to harden the server(s)?

details: danfe corp's secure software development life cycle is aligned with the build security in maturity model (bsimm). we have an sdlc policy. we require all developers to undergo annual secure code training which addresses the owasp top 10. we run weekly dast scans using the detectify web application and cloud security scanner; weekly scans also statically check for vulnerable dependencies. all pull requests for code modifications are statically analyzed for security issues via the semgrep static analysis platform, with notifications sent to the security team. we also perform threat modeling and secure code reviews for owasp top 10 on certain features. our vp of engineering, head of infra, and director of security are responsible for sdl and application security. we do not outsource software development activities.

question: what security configuration settings do you offer?
details:
the danfe corp application supports several controls for preventing and controlling access: similar to the shared responsibility model common in cloud applications, we recommend customers turn on sso (and require secure mfa at their sso provider), enable automatic user provisioning/de-provisioning using scim, disabling default public link access and monitor their activity logs for any unexpected activity. we also recommend organization admins review and approve individual plugins for use.
danfe corp’s plugin architecture is secure by design. unlike other plugin mechanisms common in rich interactive files, danfe corp plugins can only run on user activation by clicking (they cannot auto-run like macros). on activation, only one plugin can run at a time and plugins cannot persist — the user can see when the plugin is running and can stop it. plugins run heavily sandboxed/isolated and do not get arbitrary access to the user’s account or any sort of privileged access to their computer. as a result, the risk from danfe corp plugins is significantly lower than other architectures like macros. public plugins still require a review from the danfe corp team before being public. in our reviews, we check that a plugin handles data and user privacy/security expectations correctly. to prevent the malicious takeover of plugins via account takeover attacks, danfe corp requires that all plugin authors must have two-factor authentication enabled on their accounts.
nevertheless, we still recommend organizations with sophisticated security needs use the plugin allow-list functionality to control which plugins are allowed in their organization and only allow plugins after their internal review. danfe corp’s review optimizes for what's best for the broad danfe corp community and each organization might have its threat model and security/privacy goals. we recommend reviewing a plugin on its own like any other platform addon (e.g., chrome extensions are reviewed). reviews can be significantly simpler given the sandboxed execution model. further, several plugins are open-source so an organization can also review the js code for a plugin once and host them internally as a private plugin that can only be updated by the organization.

question: why does danfe corp not have dlp?

our production systems have osquery installed; additionally, our cloud infrastructure also inherits a lot of the forensics and security tooling from amazon (e.g., we have cloudtrail enabled). we have similar logging and monitoring in all our saas services and data from providers like okta, gsuite, and amazon flow into our central security data lake that has alerts set up.

details:
danfe corp has a vendor management program for selecting and overseeing all third-party services that danfe corp relies upon as part of normal business operations. the review considers risk factors such as the sensitivity of data stored in the service; the criticality of danfe corp's dependency on the service; and the reputation and history of the service, e.g. for reliability.
the vendor assessment consists of a review of the service's privacy policies and terms of service or negotiated service agreement for assertions that the service will protect and secure the data stored on the service. particularly, danfe corp looks for: a) the service will not sell, rent, transfer, distribute, or otherwise make available data stored on the service except for providing the service or for other limited reasons such as for complying with applicable laws and b) that service will take reasonable measures to secure data stored in the service.
the vendor assessment also includes a review of the vendor's information security practices which includes the following (depending on what information is made available by the vendor): soc 2 report; responses to a questionnaire submitted by danfe corp to vendors; and/or security-related information content published online by the vendor.
all third party services with which danfe corp partners have direct terms require them to adequately steward and protect customer data.
danfe corp maintains the list of vendors, data processing and protection agreements, and will share copies of subprocessor agreements based upon gdpr and contractual requirements.
note, some agreements are under nda and danfe corp may not be able to share them. danfe corp will request permission to share, but can not guarantee that the ability to share.
vendors are reviewed on a yearly cadence and the review process is revised on an ongoing basis. the vendor management process also includes subscribing and monitoring third-party dependencies for status and operational updates.

as is necessary to operate danfe corp services, operations team members have access to the servers and databases where user data is stored. for example, these employees might need to diagnose a performance issue or troubleshoot a customer-impacting error. this group of employees is limited to using a combination of employee policies and technical controls, and they are prohibited from using these permissions to view any customer data unless it is necessary to do so for operational reasons.

after a user deletes their account, information about the user and bases owned solely by that user will be deleted from production databases within 120 days. it can take up to 60 days for the data to be fully removed from all backups. danfe corp may maintain the history of customer support interactions for up to a year. for paid accounts, danfe corp retains information such as the name and email address of the payer; this information is currently retained indefinitely.

danfe corp is hosted in aws, so the production network is segregated from danfe corp employee's workstations. as is necessary to operate danfe corp services, operations team members have access to the servers and databases where user data is stored. for example, these employees might need to diagnose a performance issue or troubleshoot a customer-impacting error. this group of employees is limited to using a combination of employee policies and technical controls, and they are prohibited from using these permissions to view any customer data unless it is necessary to do so for operational reasons.
additionally, the operations team uses dedicated computers for accessing the production environment; these computers have strict policies on what software can be installed. to access the production environment via ssh, two-factor authentication is enforced by a bastion host where one authentication factor is a per-user, password-encrypted rsa-2048 ssh key, which can be individually disabled, and the other factor is a time-based, one-time password.
these passwords must have at least one each of the following: an uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, and a non-alphanumeric character. these passwords must be at least 12 characters and must not have been used for the previous 24 passwords, and must be changed every 90 days (aws enforced). two-factor authentication must be enabled and the password must be unique and never used for any other account (policy-enforced). the root aws account is not used regularly and is used only when required to perform specific aws activities that require it (such as some related to billing).

question: do you use industry standards (build security in maturity model [bsimm] benchmarks, open group acs trusted technology provider framework, nist, etc.) to build in security for your systems/software development life cycle (sdlc)?
details:
danfe corp's secure software development life cycle is closely aligned with the build security in maturity model (bsimm). role-based security awareness training for developers includes training on the owasp top 10 and the stride threat modeling methodology.
danfe corp utilizes an agile methodology for software development. as part of the development process, code and configuration changes by danfe corp developers are reviewed before being deployed. based on the nature of the change, an architecture or code-level review may be performed as deemed necessary by the cto or chief architect. the code may also receive a specific security review by the security team or danfe corp's security advisor, robert fly (former vp security engineering at salesforce).  changes are thoroughly tested before deployed.
 
as part of danfe corp's development life cycle, developers are expected to consider the possibility of threats using the stride model and to consider susceptibility to vulnerabilities described by owasp. we deliberately choose libraries and development practices to protect against cross-site scripting attacks (xss).to protect against injection attacks (specifically sql injections) danfe corp uses an object-relational mapping layer to prevent user-provided data from being used directly in sql statements. we strictly prohibit mixing user-provided data with sql statements and audit code for that. depending on the context, untrusted data must be escaped, sanitized, validated, and/or isolated. generally, the decision to implement protections and mitigations for any identified risks is based on factors such as severity, impact, risk level, trust boundaries, and tradeoffs with other concerns (such as usability).

in order to sign up for an account, an danfe corp user must provide an email address. danfe corp user's may optionally provide a name and a profile picture for their account. this data is classified as customer metadata. danfe corp does not control what information (customer data) our users store in danfe corp, so it's up to the users to decide which types of data are stored in danfe corp. danfe corp's privacy policy is availability at https://danfe corp.com/privacy and terms of service at https://danfe corp.com/tos

customer metadata is generally availability in internal tools for customer support and marketing automation. customer data is not availability in any third party customer support or marketing automation tools unless specifically sent there by the customer (e.g. by contacting support and sending in data snippets, replying to email, etc).
a limited subset of customer data (workspace, based and table names) is accessible to customer support in internal tools. danfe corp is a general-purpose productivity tool and doesn't control the type of information that a user enters into a based. for specific details of the type of data that will be handle, please reach out to the end user for further details on the data they plan to enter into danfe corp.
as is necessary to operate danfe corp services, a deliberately small number of technical employees have access the servers and databases where user data is stored. for example, these employees might need to diagnose a performance issue or troubleshoot a customer-impacting error. this group of employees is limited using a combination of employee policies and technical controls, and they are prohibited from using these permissions to view any customer data unless it is necessary to do so for operational reasons. to access the production environment via ssh, two-factor authentication is enforced by a bastion host where one authentication factor is a per-user password-encrypted rsa-2048 ssh key, which can be individually disabled, and the other factor is a time-based one-time password.
the danfe corp service generates network, audit, application, event, server, and other logs. depending on the type of log events, the logs are collected either in the danfe corp service's databases or in s3. in both cases, access to the log files is limited operations team members, and audit trails for the logs files themselves are maintained by aws cloudtrail. log buckets are protected based on best practices including create-only access, bucket versioning, and aws's "mfa delete" is enabled. security-related events and logs are streamed to aws cloudwatch and notifications are created for and monitoring by members of danfe corp's operations team.

all third party services with which danfe corp partners have direct terms require them to adequately steward and protect customer data. the following describes danfe corp's vendor management program.
danfe corp has a vendor management program for selecting and overseeing the third-party services that danfe corp relies upon as part of normal business operations. the review considers risk factors such as the sensitivity of data stored in the service, the criticality of danfe corp's dependency on the service, and the reputation and history of the service, e.g. for reliability. the vendor assessment consists of a review of the service's privacy policies and terms of service or negotiated service agreement for assertions that the service will protect and secure the data stored on the service. particularly, danfe corp looks for: a) the service will not sell, rent, transfer, distribute, or otherwise make available data stored on the service except for providing the service or for other limited reasons such as for complying with applicable laws and b) that service will take reasonable measures to secure data stored in the service. the vendor assessment also includes a review of the vendor's information security practices which includes the following (depending on what information is made available by the vendor): soc 2 report; responses to a questionnaire submitted by danfe corp to vendors; and/or security-related information content published online by the vendor.
vendors are reviewed on a yearly cadence and the review process is revised on an ongoing basis. the vendor management process also includes subscribing and monitoring third-party dependencies for status and operational updates.
danfe corp carries insurance that covers subcontractor vicarious liability.

question: are file integrity (host) and network intrusion detection (ids) tools implemented to help facilitate timely detection, investigation by root cause analysis and response to incidents?
details:
danfe corp runs aws guard duty in production to monitor for intrusions. when an alert occurs, a notification is sent to danfe corp's operations team which is on call 24x7x365. danfe corp also utilizes a commercial web application firewall (waf) from signal sciences.
danfe corp enforces file integrity when new hosts are rebuilt as part of the weekly deploy process, but danfe corp does not actively monitor file integrity. danfe corp source code is hosted on github and communication is protected from tampering by use of tls or ssl.
danfe corp verifies checksums for all dependencies installed during the weekly deploy process. it's on danfe corp's security roadmap to implement additional integrity checking on software running on production systems.
danfe corp's services run in isolated vpc with strict controls over allowed ingress and egress rules. the rules are enforced at both the security group and the vpc level. danfe corp minimizes public-facing exposure of the infrastructure to only strictly necessary ports; allow access to internal infrastructure only via a bastion host with two-factor authentication at the ssh level. danfe corp aligns hardening efforts with the center for internet security (cis) benchmark for aws.
danfe corp takes an "immutable infrastructure" approach to infrastructure and rebuilds a new production stack during the weekly blue-green deploy process so that the application is built from the ground up in the production environment. danfe corp verifies checksums for all dependencies installed during the weekly deploy process.
as part of building new servers, danfe corp hardens os using steps such as: launching new machines in a protected network environment, restricting user accounts and privileges, and updating packages to receive the latest patches.

question: do you use industry standards (build security in maturity model [bsimm] benchmarks, open group acs trusted technology provider framework, nist, etc.) to build in security for your systems/software development life cycle (sdlc)?
details:
danfe corp's secure software development life cycle is closely aligned with the build security in maturity model (bsimm). role-based security awareness training for developers includes training on the owasp top 10 and the stride threat modeling methodology.
danfe corp utilizes an agile methodology for software development. as part of the development process, code and configuration changes by danfe corp developers are reviewed before being deployed. based on the nature of the change, an architecture or code-level review may be performed as deemed necessary by the cto or chief architect. the code may also receive a specific security review by the security team or danfe corp's security advisor, robert fly (former vp security engineering at salesforce).  changes are thoroughly tested before deployed.
 
as part of danfe corp's development life cycle, developers are expected to consider the possibility of threats using the stride model and to consider susceptibility to vulnerabilities described by owasp. we deliberately choose libraries and development practices to protect against cross-site scripting attacks (xss).to protect against injection attacks (specifically sql injections) danfe corp uses an object-relational mapping layer to prevent user-provided data from being used directly in sql statements. we strictly prohibit mixing user-provided data with sql statements and audit code for that. depending on the context, untrusted data must be escaped, sanitized, validated, and/or isolated. generally, the decision to implement protections and mitigations for any identified risks is based on factors such as severity, impact, risk level, trust boundaries, and tradeoffs with other concerns (such as usability).

question: is there a periodic (at least annual) review of your business resiliency program?
is there a data classification retention program that identifies the data types that require additional management and governance?
details:
danfe corp maintains internal acceptable use policies and role-specific training. danfe corp utilizes role-based access control and the principle of least privilege for granting access. when new employees are added or when existing employees change roles, the employee's role determines which systems they are granted access to and at what access level. access privileges are reviewed at least yearly and when an employee changes roles or status.
danfe corp also maintains a disciplinary process for non-compliance with security-related policies.
as is necessary to operate danfe corp services, operations team members have access to the servers and databases where user data is stored. for example, these employees might need to diagnose a performance issue or troubleshoot a customer-impacting error. this group of employees is limited to using a combination of employee policies and technical controls, and they are prohibited from using these permissions to view any customer data unless it is necessary to do so for operational reasons.
additionally, the operations team uses dedicated computers for accessing the production environment; these computers have strict policies on what software can be installed. to access the production environment via ssh, two-factor authentication is enforced by a bastion host where one authentication factor is a per-user password-encrypted rsa-2048 ssh key, which can be individually disabled, and the other factor is a time-based one-time password.
these passwords must have at least one each of the following: an uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, non-alphanumeric character. these passwords must be at least 12 characters and must not have been used for the previous 24 passwords, and must be changed every 90 days (aws enforced). two-factor authentication must be enabled and the password must be unique and never used for any other account (policy-enforced). the root aws account is not used on a regular basis and is used only when required to perform specific aws activities that require it (such as some related to billing).

question: are firewalls used to isolate critical and sensitive systems into network segments separate from network segments with less sensitive systems?
details: danfe corp's production environment uses amazon vpc for network segmentation. public access is only availability into a dmz running only public load balancers and our internal access bastion. all services are in the private part that is not accessible to the public. the internal network is further segmented by function (web, workers, db).

question: is there a vendor management program?
details:

danfe corp maintains internal acceptable use policies and role-specific training. danfe corp utilizes role-based access control and the principle of least privilege for granting access. when new employees are added or when existing employees change roles, the employee's role determines which systems they are granted access to and at what access level. access privileges are reviewed at least yearly and when an employee changes roles or status.
danfe corp also maintains a disciplinary process for non-compliance with security-related policies.
as is necessary to operate danfe corp services, operations team members have access to the servers and databases where user data is stored. for example, these employees might need to diagnose a performance issue or troubleshoot a customer-impacting error. this group of employees is limited to using a combination of employee policies and technical controls, and they are prohibited from using these permissions to view any customer data unless it is necessary to do so for operational reasons.
additionally, the operations team uses dedicated computers for accessing the production environment; these computers have strict policies on what software can be installed. to access the production environment via ssh, two-factor authentication is enforced by a bastion host where one authentication factor is a per-user password-encrypted rsa-2048 ssh key, which can be individually disabled, and the other factor is a time-based one-time password.

access policies

question: please upload your data encryption standard.

question: how do you train developers in ssdlc / secure coding practices?
details:
danfe corp utilizes an agile methodology for software development. as part of the development process, code, and configuration changes by danfe corp developers are reviewed before being deployed. based on the nature of the change, architecture or code-level review may be performed as deemed necessary by the cto or chief architect. the code may also receive a specific security review by the security team or danfe corp's security advisor, robert fly (former vp security engineering at salesforce). changes are thoroughly tested before deployed.
as part of danfe corp's development life cycle, developers are expected to consider the possibility of threats using the stride model and to consider susceptibility to vulnerabilities described by owasp. we deliberately choose libraries and development practices to protect against cross-site scripting attacks (xss).to protect against injection attacks (specifically sql injections) danfe corp uses an object-relational mapping layer to prevent user-provided data from being used directly in sql statements. we strictly prohibit mixing user-provided data with sql statements and audit code for that. depending on the context, untrusted data must be escaped, sanitized, validated, and/or isolated. generally, the decision to implement protections and mitigations for any identified risks is based on factors such as severity, impact, risk level, trust boundaries, and tradeoffs with other concerns (such as usability).

question: do you have controls to manage malware/malicious code? describe.
details:
we minimize the software installed and weigh any additional tools against the possibility of accidental or malicious data exposure. the software running on the servers is tightly controlled and monitored.
our production systems are closely controlled. all configuration and installed software are code-reviewed. we utilize an agile methodology for software development. as part of the development process, code, and configuration changes by our developers are reviewed before being deployed. based on the nature of the change, an architecture or code-level review may be performed as deemed necessary by the cto or chief architect. the code may also receive a specific security review by the security team or by one of our security advisors, robert fly (former vp security engineering at salesforce) or diogo mónica (docker security lead).
 
changes are thoroughly tested before being deployed. as part of the quality assurance process for every update, acceptance testing is performed on multiple operating systems and browsers to ensure a consistent experience across all devices, platforms, and browsers that are supported by us.
 
as part of our development life cycle, developers are expected to consider the possibility of threats using the stride model and to consider susceptibility to vulnerabilities described by owasp. we deliberately choose libraries and development practices to protect against cross-site scripting attacks (xss).to protect against injection attacks (specifically sql injections) we use an object-relational mapping layer to prevent user-provided data from being used directly in sql statements. we strictly prohibit mixing user-provided data with sql statements and audit code for that. depending on the context, untrusted data must be escaped, sanitized, validated, and/or isolated. generally, the decision to implement protections and mitigations for any identified risks is based on factors such as severity, impact, risk level, trust boundaries, and tradeoffs with other concerns (such as usability).
we take an immutable infrastructure approach to infrastructure and we rebuild a new production stack during our weekly blue-green deploy process so that the application is built from the ground up in our production environment. we verify checksums for all dependencies installed during our weekly deploy process.
 
as part of building new servers, we harden os using steps such as: launching new machines in a protected network environment; restricting user accounts and privileges; updating packages to receive the latest patches.
 
our aws environment aligns with the cis amazon web services foundations benchmark level 2.

these passwords must have at least one each of the following: an uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, non-alphanumeric character. these passwords must be at least 12 characters and must not have been used for the previous 24 passwords, and must be changed every 90 days (aws enforced). two-factor authentication must be enabled and the password must be unique and never used for any other account (policy-enforced). the root aws account is not used regularly and is used only when required to perform specific aws activities that require it (such as some related to billing).
